**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

questions.enonce_markdown: Substantiate with at least five features, the fact that African Traditional Religions is a "Religion" on its own merit. (25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Early outside writers often called African beliefs "paganism", "animism" or "fetishism" and denied that they were a real religion. Modern scholars such as John Mbiti and Bolaji Idowu argue that African Traditional Religion (ATR) is a genuine religion with its own beliefs, practices and values. The features below, which are general and vary among peoples, support this.

**1. Belief in a Supreme Being.** Most African peoples know a creator and sustainer, often with names such as Nyame (Akan), Olodumare (Yoruba) or Chukwu (Igbo). He is the source of life and moral order, approached in prayer, proverbs and names.

**2. Belief in divinities and spirits.** Beside the Supreme Being there are lesser divinities and spirits, associated with rivers, land, sky, trees or human activities, who act as agents or intermediaries.

**3. Veneration of ancestors.** The dead who are remembered are believed to remain members of the family, guarding it and mediating between the living and God. They are honoured by libation and offerings.

**4. Worship, prayer and sacrifice.** ATR has regular acts of worship: prayers, libation, offerings, sacrifices of food or animals, and dances, in order to thank, ask help or restore harmony.

**5. Sacred places, objects and persons.** Shrines, groves, rivers, hills and symbols are respected, and there are religious specialists: priests, diviners, rain-makers and medicine men.

**6. Festivals and rites of passage.** Birth, naming, puberty and initiation, marriage and death are marked by religious rites, as are agricultural and seasonal festivals.

**7. Moral code and taboos.** Right and wrong are defined by the community and are believed to be sanctioned by the Supreme Being, divinities and ancestors. Breaking a taboo requires purification.

**8. Belief in life after death and the spirit world.** Death is a passage to another state of existence.

**9. Oral transmission.** The religion is passed on by myths, proverbs, songs, praise names, rituals and customs rather than by written scriptures.

**Answering objections.** ATR has no single founder or book and is not a missionary religion, but this does not stop it being a religion: its members hold coherent beliefs and perform acts of worship that give meaning to life. It differs from other religions in form but not in kind.

**Conclusion.** With belief in God, spiritual beings, ancestors, worship, sacred places and persons, rites, ethics and oral tradition, ATR meets the usual criteria of a religion on its own merit.
